takeaways: Build your eman on reflection and evidence, not only on what you inherited.
Actively listen to and reflect on the signs of Allah around you.
Learn your deen from living teachers and scholars, not only from screens.
Take the prophets, and above all Muhammad, as concrete role models in how you live.
Turn faith into action: enjoy what Allah provides, pay its zakat and do not waste.

6:66.ar: وَكَذَّبَ بِهِۦ قَوۡمُكَ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَقُّۚ قُل لَّسۡتُ عَلَيۡكُم بِوَكِيلࣲ‏
6:66.en: Thy people (O Muhammad) have denied it, though it is the Truth. Say: I am not put in charge of you

10:99.ar: وَلَوۡ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لَأٓمَنَ مَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ كُلُّهُمۡ جَمِيعًاۚ أَفَأَنتَ تُكۡرِهُ ٱلنَّاسَ حَتَّىٰ يَكُونُواْ مُؤۡمِنِينَ
10:99.en: And if thy Lord willed, all who are in the earth would have believed together. Wouldst thou (Muhammad) compel men until they are believers

17:1.ar: سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَسۡرَىٰ بِعَبۡدِهِۦ لَيۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ إِلَى ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡأَقۡصَا ٱلَّذِي بَٰرَكۡنَا حَوۡلَهُۥ لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَآۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
17:1.en: Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far distant place of worship the neighbourhood whereof We have blessed, that We might show him of Our tokens! Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Seer

59:9.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ يُحِبُّونَ مَنۡ هَاجَرَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ حَاجَةࣰ مِّمَّآ أُوتُواْ وَيُؤۡثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَلَوۡ كَانَ بِهِمۡ خَصَاصَةࣱۚ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
59:9.en: Those who entered the city and the faith before them love those who flee unto them for refuge, and find in their breasts no need for that which hath been given them, but prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot. And whoso is saved from his own avarice - such are they who are successful

2:264.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُبۡطِلُواْ صَدَقَٰتِكُم بِٱلۡمَنِّ وَٱلۡأَذَىٰ كَٱلَّذِي يُنفِقُ مَالَهُۥ رِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۖ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ صَفۡوَانٍ عَلَيۡهِ تُرَابࣱ فَأَصَابَهُۥ وَابِلࣱ فَتَرَكَهُۥ صَلۡدࣰ اۖ لَّا يَقۡدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَيۡءࣲ مِّمَّا كَسَبُواْۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:264.en: O ye who believe! Render not vain your almsgiving by reproach and injury, like him who spendeth his wealth only to be seen of men and believeth not in Allah and the Last Day. His likeness is as the likeness of a rock whereon is dust of earth; a rainstorm smiteth it, leaving it smooth and bare. They have no control of aught of that which they have gained. Allah guideth not the disbelieving folk

-ohq34i_7h0.speaker: adnan
-ohq34i_7h0.speaker_note: continues his own Ramadan values series from the previous night on responsibility and stewardship
-ohq34i_7h0.title: The Values of Islam: Khidmah (Service) and Ithar (Selflessness)
-ohq34i_7h0.one_line: Being Allah's servant means serving others, not controlling them, and selflessness, aimed at the Hereafter, keeps service sincere, quiet and beneficial.
-ohq34i_7h0.summary: The sheikh argues that Islamic values come as a package: losing one makes a person unethical, so the list has never changed. Service and selflessness complete responsibility and stewardship. Linguistically, 'abd evokes lowliness, a top level of love in Arabic poetry, and someone brought in to serve, so 'ibadah is best understood as service. A servant does not control or coerce; Allah Himself left people free, and the prophets said they were not wardens over their people, a lesson for those in da'wah. Without selflessness, service becomes performance, a way to look virtuous or create dependency, and people naturally want to be served. Selflessness is not self-destruction but transcending the ego, with self-interest redirected toward the Hereafter, as in the Ansari couple who fed a guest in the dark while their children slept hungry. Doing good only to feel good fails once people repay service with betrayal. Outcomes also matter: service that breeds laziness, as with over-serving children, is misplaced. The Prophet gave and walked away but always remembered favours done to him. He calls for quiet service in the trenches, against the culture of views and likes, and asks each person to find their domain of service.

outline.heading: Values come in packages
outline.gist: Islamic values do not exist in silos; take them all or slowly lose them all.

outline.heading: One breach makes you unethical
outline.gist: Being ethical requires every value, while losing one, such as honesty, is enough to be unethical.

outline.heading: An unchanging list
outline.gist: The list has been stable since Adam; service and selflessness complement responsibility and stewardship.

outline.heading: We are servants whether we like it or not
outline.gist: The only question is whether we are good servants; 'abd linguistically evokes level, trodden ground.

outline.heading: 'Ubudiyyah as a level of love
outline.gist: Among the Arabs' levels of love, enslavement to the beloved is near the top.

outline.heading: 'Ibadah means service
outline.gist: A servant is brought in to serve, so worship is in essence service, and that is how stewardship is fulfilled.

outline.heading: Not a controller over people
outline.gist: The prophets said they were not wardens; if Allah did not force people, those in da'wah have no business coercing them.

outline.heading: Servants do not enforce
outline.gist: Collective law is legitimate, but an individual servant's role is to offer service, not impose rules.

outline.heading: Service without selflessness is performance
outline.gist: People serve to look virtuous, control or create loyalty; selflessness purifies the motive and gives ethical coherence.

outline.heading: We want to be served
outline.gist: People climb ladders so others will serve them, while the goal is to benefit others as much as possible.

outline.heading: Islam simplified, and masjids as places of service
outline.gist: Masjids should see people walking in as opportunities to serve, not as donors.

outline.heading: The Prophet served day and night
outline.gist: He met every need he could; a servant cannot be arrogant or controlling.

outline.heading: 'His servant' as the highest praise
outline.gist: Scholars see Allah calling the Prophet His 'abd as the greatest praise he received.

outline.heading: Selflessness is transcending the ego
outline.gist: Islam never asks you to destroy or neglect yourself, only to get past the ego.

outline.heading: Be selfish for the Hereafter
outline.gist: Islam redirects self-interest toward one's status on the Day of Judgment, reached through selflessness here.

outline.heading: The Ansari couple and their guest
outline.gist: They put the children to sleep and pretended to eat in the dark so the guest would eat, and the verse on preferring others was revealed.

outline.heading: I do this for me
outline.gist: He teaches for his own reward with Allah; claiming to want nothing at all hides a wish to feel virtuous.

outline.heading: When serving stops feeling good
outline.gist: People betray and mistreat those who serve them; only hope in Allah's recognition keeps service going.

outline.heading: Outcomes matter
outline.gist: Service that creates dependency or laziness, as in parents over-serving children, is misplaced.

outline.heading: Give and walk away
outline.gist: Reminding people of favours ruins the deed; the Prophet never mentioned his gifts but always repaid favours.

outline.heading: Avoiding recognition
outline.gist: Praise and repayment may consume the reward, so keep serving in many unnoticed ways.

outline.heading: Service as love, selflessness as a transparent ego
outline.gist: Together they produce moral maturity that is quietly transformative.

outline.heading: Working in the trenches
outline.gist: The true worker avoids attention and slowly changes the status quo.

outline.heading: The Prophet's quiet transformation
outline.gist: His selfless service transformed people one by one until they joined the same work.

outline.heading: Views, likes and clicks
outline.gist: Words that meant nothing fifteen years ago now drive a hunger for being seen.

outline.heading: Find your domain of service
outline.gist: Serve the ummah and Allah quietly, wanting nothing from people; this is Islam in a nutshell.

themes.label: Service (khidmah) and servanthood
themes.note: 'Ibadah understood as service; a servant serves rather than controls.

themes.label: Selfishness, greed of the soul (shuhh) and selflessness
themes.note: Selflessness as ego-transcendence with self-interest aimed at the Hereafter.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Serve for Allah's reward, not to feel good, be praised or be repaid.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Those in public work drift toward control and coercion, which is not the prophetic way.

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: Values form a package; one breach is enough to be unethical.

themes.label: Technology, AI, social media and attention
themes.note: The culture of views and likes against quiet service.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: He served constantly and was praised as Allah's servant.

quran.point: Prophets saying they are not wardens or controllers over their people.
Had Allah willed He would have compelled belief; no one else may force people.
The Prophet described as Allah's servant, seen as the highest praise.
They prefer others over themselves even when in need.
Do not void charity with reminders of it.

hadith.gist: An Ansari took the Prophet's starving guest home; he and his wife put their children to sleep and pretended to eat in the dark; the Prophet told him Allah admired what they did.
The Prophet would give and tell the person to take it and go, yet would repeatedly remind people of favours they had done him and try to repay them.

maxims: We're all servants; are you a good one or a bad one?
Selfless in dunya, selfish for the akhirah
Selflessness is the transcendence of ego
Quietly transformative, in the trenches
To be unethical, all it takes is one

stories.who: The Ansari couple who fed the Prophet's guest
stories.point: True selflessness hides itself so the other can benefit without shame.

contemporary: Social media culture of views, likes and clicks
Masjids treating attendees as donors
Restaurants and hotels as the pursuit of being served
takeaways: Find your own domain of service and commit to it quietly
Serve without seeking control, recognition or repayment
Never remind people of what you did for them
Check the outcome of your service so it does not create dependency or laziness
Aim your self-interest at Allah's reward so service survives ingratitude

7:175.ar: وَٱتۡلُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ نَبَأَ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ ءَايَٰتِنَا فَٱنسَلَخَ مِنۡهَا فَأَتۡبَعَهُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ فَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَاوِينَ
7:175.en: Recite unto them the tale of him to whom We gave Our revelations, but he sloughed them off, so Satan overtook him and he became of those who lead astray

7:176.ar: وَلَوۡ شِئۡنَا لَرَفَعۡنَٰهُ بِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّهُۥٓ أَخۡلَدَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُۚ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ ٱلۡكَلۡبِ إِن تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡهِ يَلۡهَثۡ أَوۡ تَتۡرُكۡهُ يَلۡهَثۚ ذَّٰلِكَ مَثَلُ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَاۚ فَٱقۡصُصِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
7:176.en: And had We willed We could have raised him by their means, but he clung to the earth and followed his own lust. Therefor his likeness is as the likeness of a dog: if thou attackest him he panteth with his tongue out, and if thou leavest him he panteth with his tongue out. Such is the likeness of the people who deny Our revelations. Narrate unto them the history (of the men of old), that haply they may take thought

7:177.ar: سَآءَ مَثَلًا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَأَنفُسَهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَظۡلِمُونَ
7:177.en: Evil as an example are the folk who denied Our revelations, and were wont to wrong themselves

7:178.ar: مَن يَهۡدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدِيۖ وَمَن يُضۡلِلۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
7:178.en: He whom Allah leadeth, he indeed is led aright, while he whom Allah sendeth astray - they indeed are losers

8:42.ar: إِذۡ أَنتُم بِٱلۡعُدۡوَةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَهُم بِٱلۡعُدۡوَةِ ٱلۡقُصۡوَىٰ وَٱلرَّكۡبُ أَسۡفَلَ مِنكُمۡۚ وَلَوۡ تَوَاعَدتُّمۡ لَٱخۡتَلَفۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡمِيعَٰدِ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَقۡضِيَ ٱللَّهُ أَمۡرࣰ ا كَانَ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا لِّيَهۡلِكَ مَنۡ هَلَكَ عَنۢ بَيِّنَةࣲ وَيَحۡيَىٰ مَنۡ حَيَّ عَنۢ بَيِّنَةࣲۗ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَسَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
8:42.en: When ye were on the near bank (of the valley) and they were on the yonder bank, and the caravan was below you (on the coast plain). And had ye trysted to meet one another ye surely would have failed to keep the tryst, but (it happened, as it did, without the forethought of either of you) that Allah might conclude a thing that must be done; that he who perished (on that day) might perish by a clear proof (of His Sovereignty) and he who survived might survive by a clear proof (of His Sovereignty). Lo! Allah in truth is Hearer, Knower

8:43.ar: إِذۡ يُرِيكَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَنَامِكَ قَلِيلࣰ اۖ وَلَوۡ أَرَىٰكَهُمۡ كَثِيرࣰ ا لَّفَشِلۡتُمۡ وَلَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَلَّمَۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
8:43.en: When Allah showed them unto thee (O Muhammad) in thy dream as few in number, and if He had shown them to thee as many, ye (Muslims) would have faltered and would have quarrelled over the affair. But Allah saved (you). Lo! He knoweth what is in the breasts (of men)

8:44.ar: وَإِذۡ يُرِيكُمُوهُمۡ إِذِ ٱلۡتَقَيۡتُمۡ فِيٓ أَعۡيُنِكُمۡ قَلِيلࣰ ا وَيُقَلِّلُكُمۡ فِيٓ أَعۡيُنِهِمۡ لِيَقۡضِيَ ٱللَّهُ أَمۡرࣰ ا كَانَ مَفۡعُولࣰ اۗ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
8:44.en: And when He made you (Muslims), when ye met (them), see them with your eyes as few, and lessened you in their eyes, (it was) that Allah might conclude a thing that must be done. Unto Allah all things are brought back

9:25.ar: لَقَدۡ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةࣲ وَيَوۡمَ حُنَيۡنٍ إِذۡ أَعۡجَبَتۡكُمۡ كَثۡرَتُكُمۡ فَلَمۡ تُغۡنِ عَنكُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتۡ ثُمَّ وَلَّيۡتُم مُّدۡبِرِينَ
9:25.en: Allah hath given you victory on many fields and on the day of Huneyn, when ye exulted in your multitude but it availed you naught, and the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for you; then ye turned back in flight

9:26.ar: ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِۦ وَعَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَأَنزَلَ جُنُودࣰ ا لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَا وَعَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۚ وَذَٰلِكَ جَزَآءُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
9:26.en: Then Allah sent His peace of reassurance down upon His messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts ye could not see, and punished those who disbelieved. Such is the reward of disbelievers

9:27.ar: ثُمَّ يَتُوبُ ٱللَّهُ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
9:27.en: Then afterward Allah will relent toward whom He will; for Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

kLPogxbE1cU.speaker: adnan
kLPogxbE1cU.speaker_note: Sh. Adnan's Ramadan halqa series; speaks of his father moving to Canada and growing up in Medina
kLPogxbE1cU.title: Receiving Allah's Bounty (Ramadan 2026, Night 9: Quranic Themes 2)
kLPogxbE1cU.one_line: Three Quranic passages on how people receive Allah's bounty: the man who shed Allah's signs, the hidden arrangement of Badr, and the vanity of Hunayn.
kLPogxbE1cU.summary: He frames the night around how people respond when Allah gives them something good. The first passage describes a man granted Allah's signs who wriggled out of them the way a snake sheds its skin, and who clung to the earth and his appetites when he could have been raised. The image of the dog that pants whether resting or working teaches that life is tiring on every path, so it makes no sense to choose the inferior one. Anyone who knows the Quran and sunnah has received this gift; it is not a burden or a license to judge others, and it can be taken back. The Badr verses show bounty in things no one could plan: where each army stood when the rain fell, a dream that showed the enemy as few, and how each army perceived the other. He invites the audience to look back at their own lives, as he does at his own family history, and see how much was arranged for them, and to stay thankful without bragging, as the people of Badr did. Hunayn shows the opposite: the companions took comfort in their numbers and nearly lost everything. He warns against measuring the deen, the masjid or one's security by numbers or bank balances, while still using numbers as feedback.

outline.heading: What it means to receive Allah's bounty
outline.gist: Bounty here means ease and what people hope for; he mentions a dua asking Allah to keep favouring us rather than test us, since we are weak, and introduces a passage that weighs most on people of religious knowledge.

outline.heading: The man who slipped out of Allah's signs
outline.gist: Allah tells of a man given His ayat; the verb pictures a snake shedding its skin or a child squirming out of a jacket. He leaves the attached story of a scholar of Bani Israel for another session.

outline.heading: He could have been raised but clung to the earth
outline.gist: The signs could have elevated him, but he sank to the ground like a mole and chose food, status, fame and desire over a life of selflessness and service.

outline.heading: The panting dog: life is tiring either way
outline.gist: A dog pants whether resting or working; you cannot be neutral in life and no path is free of hardship, so choose one with good meaning.

outline.heading: Choosing the inferior life over the gift
outline.gist: Quran, sunnah, Ramadan, family and purpose are on offer, yet people chase what others seem to enjoy on yachts and at parties. Everyone listening has been given enough of the ayat to know right from wrong.

outline.heading: The ayat are a gift that can be withdrawn
outline.gist: Knowledge of the deen is not a reason for arrogance, self-righteousness or judging people, nor a burden. Gifts must be honoured or they are taken back, as with people who lost their closeness to the masjid without knowing how.

outline.heading: Badr: a meeting no one could have arranged
outline.gist: The caravan escaped and the Muslims faced Quraysh on the near side of the valley; had they tried to set this appointment it would never have lined up, but Allah had decreed it.

outline.heading: Rain on rock and rain on sand
outline.gist: The rain firmed the rocky ground under the Muslims and turned the enemy's sandy ground to mud, a detail none of them had planned.

outline.heading: The dream that showed the enemy as few
outline.gist: Outnumbered three to one in the Prophet's first battle, the Muslims rested before fighting and the Prophet saw the enemy as fewer in his dream, which lifted his spirits.

outline.heading: Even the people of Badr could have faltered
outline.gist: Had Allah shown them many, even these best of companions would have lost heart and disputed; Allah alone protected them, and he notes how striking it is that the Quran says this of them.

outline.heading: Each army saw the other as few
outline.gist: Allah controls how the brain perceives what the eye sees: every Muslim saw the enemy as fewer, and Quraysh saw the Muslims as few and became sloppy.

outline.heading: Bounty in what you never notice
outline.gist: Allah's bounty is not only a car or a job; it can be a perception, a small dream, or events lined up better than you could have arranged.

outline.heading: Looking back over a life
outline.gist: With age and reflection people see how easily things could have gone wrong; he points to his father coming to Canada, his mother's conversion and the family's move to Medina as Allah's arrangement.

outline.heading: The people of Badr never bragged
outline.gist: They only said they witnessed that day, crediting it all to Allah and staying thankful.

outline.heading: Hunayn: twelve thousand strong
outline.gist: Always outnumbered before, the Muslims at Hunayn numbered about twelve thousand and felt the battle would be easy.

outline.heading: Quality, not quantity
outline.gist: Their numbers made them vain. In the deen one person of real character or scholarship outweighs an arena of indifferent people, yet masajid still measure success by attendance.

outline.heading: The near-defeat at Hunayn
outline.gist: Even at half the enemy's strength they leaned on numbers and were routed; the Prophet was left almost alone and nearly killed until his uncle called the companions back.

outline.heading: Do not lean on numbers or wealth
outline.gist: Do not feel secure because of numbers or a bank balance; the One who provides keeps caring for you. Numbers are useful only as feedback on whether you are doing a good job.

themes.label: Guidance (hidayah)
themes.note: The man given Allah's signs who threw them off; knowing the Quran and sunnah is a gift that raises you if honoured and is withdrawn if rejected.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Life is hard on every path, like the dog that pants at rest and at work, so choose the path with meaning over chasing appetites.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: Badr as a battle arranged by Allah through terrain, rain, a dream and perception; Hunayn as a near-defeat caused by confidence in numbers.

themes.label: Divine decree and Allah's hidden arrangement

12:31.ar: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتۡ بِمَكۡرِهِنَّ أَرۡسَلَتۡ إِلَيۡهِنَّ وَأَعۡتَدَتۡ لَهُنَّ مُتَّكَـࣰٔ ا وَءَاتَتۡ كُلَّ وَٰحِدَةࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ سِكِّينࣰ ا وَقَالَتِ ٱخۡرُجۡ عَلَيۡهِنَّۖ فَلَمَّا رَأَيۡنَهُۥٓ أَكۡبَرۡنَهُۥ وَقَطَّعۡنَ أَيۡدِيَهُنَّ وَقُلۡنَ حَٰشَ لِلَّهِ مَا هَٰذَا بَشَرًا إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا مَلَكࣱ كَرِيمࣱ‏
12:31.en: And when she heard of their sly talk, she sent to them and prepared for them a cushioned couch (to lie on at the feast) and gave to every one of them a knife and said (to Joseph): Come out unto them! And when they saw him they exalted him and cut their hands, exclaiming: Allah Blameless! This is no a human being. This is not other than some gracious angel

12:32.ar: قَالَتۡ فَذَٰلِكُنَّ ٱلَّذِي لُمۡتُنَّنِي فِيهِۖ وَلَقَدۡ رَٰوَدتُّهُۥ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦ فَٱسۡتَعۡصَمَۖ وَلَئِن لَّمۡ يَفۡعَلۡ مَآ ءَامُرُهُۥ لَيُسۡجَنَنَّ وَلَيَكُونࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ
12:32.en: She said: This is he on whose account ye blamed me. I asked of him an evil act, but he proved continent, but if he do not my behest he verily shall be imprisoned, and verily shall be of those brought low

12:33.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱلسِّجۡنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدۡعُونَنِيٓ إِلَيۡهِۖ وَإِلَّا تَصۡرِفۡ عَنِّي كَيۡدَهُنَّ أَصۡبُ إِلَيۡهِنَّ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِينَ
12:33.en: He said: O my Lord! Prison is more dear than that unto which they urge me, and if Thou fend not off their wiles from me I shall incline unto them and become of the foolish

12:108.ar: قُلۡ هَٰذِهِۦ سَبِيلِيٓ أَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۚ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا۠ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِيۖ وَسُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
12:108.en: Say: This is my Way: I call on Allah with sure knowledge. I and whosoever followeth me - Glory be to Allah! - and I am not of the idolaters

13:28.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَتَطۡمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُم بِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۗ أَلَا بِذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطۡمَئِنُّ ٱلۡقُلُوبُ
13:28.en: Who have believed and whose hearts have rest in the remembrance of Allah. Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest

62:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي بَعَثَ فِي ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏

12:23.ar: وَرَٰوَدَتۡهُ ٱلَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيۡتِهَا عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦ وَغَلَّقَتِ ٱلۡأَبۡوَٰبَ وَقَالَتۡ هَيۡتَ لَكَۚ قَالَ مَعَاذَ ٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ رَبِّيٓ أَحۡسَنَ مَثۡوَايَۖ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
12:23.en: And she, in whose house he was, asked of him an evil act. She bolted the doors and said: Come! He said: I seek refuge in Allah! Lo! he is my lord, who hath treated me honourably. Lo! wrong-doers never prosper

12:91.ar: قَالُواْ تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدۡ ءَاثَرَكَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَإِن كُنَّا لَخَٰطِـِٔينَ
12:91.en: They said: By Allah, verily Allah hath preferred thee above us, and we were indeed sinful

12:92.ar: قَالَ لَا تَثۡرِيبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ يَغۡفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
12:92.en: He said: Have no fear this day! May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy

4bf30rcAWH0.title: Finding Serenity in Allah (Ramadan 2026, Night 12: Quranic Themes 2)
4bf30rcAWH0.one_line: Serenity in Allah through Yusuf choosing prison over sin, the Prophet calling with clear insight, and hearts finding rest in Allah's remembrance.
4bf30rcAWH0.summary: He calls serenity in Allah one of the Quran's major themes and a main purpose of knowing Him: the spirit needs nourishment from a real relationship with Allah, and like a child learning to eat it grows through clumsy steps, which Ramadan's nightly prayers train. Once that relationship is found, a Muslim lives out the meaning rather than searching for it. Yusuf, pursued by a powerful woman and the women of the city and threatened with prison, said prison was dearer to him than sin; he spent years jailed unjustly without regret, showing that inner peace no enemy can touch. He contrasts this with Muslims who joke they would trade jail time for a night of sin, explains the rules between the sexes as protection for human weakness, warns young people about texting and private chats that lead to unwise marriages, and urges them not to spoil their chastity by fantasising about haram. Verse 12:108 shows the Prophet calling to Allah with calm insight, which he lived when Abu Sufyan came to him with the words of Yusuf's brothers and was forgiven. The night ends with 13:28: hearts find rest only in Allah's remembrance, which is what the masjid is for and how one faces problems calmly.

outline.heading: Four surahs, four domains of faith
outline.gist: Recap of the cluster: each surah takes a critical element of a domain, such as reform in the message, consistency in ethics and righteousness in law; tonight finishes the cluster.

outline.heading: Serenity in Allah: a major Quranic theme
outline.gist: He ranks themes by how often the Quran returns to them; finding tranquility and peace of heart in Allah is one of the major ones and a main purpose of knowing Him.

outline.heading: The spirit learns to eat like a child
outline.gist: Food nourishes the body, but the spirit is nourished only by a genuine relationship with Allah, which grows through baby steps and mistakes whether you start at six or sixty.

outline.heading: Ramadan as a boot camp for the heart
outline.gist: Nightly prayer lets you practise focus and closeness; some nights go well and others do not, so embrace the struggle and build the capacity to connect.

outline.heading: Found meaning, now live it
outline.gist: Prophets were sent to recite Allah's signs so people would know Him; once you have that relationship, life is about acting on the meaning you found, not still searching for it.

outline.heading: The banquet: the women see Yusuf
outline.gist: Gossip spread about the minister's wife pursuing Yusuf, so she invited the women and they cut their hands at the sight of him; the Prophet said after the Night Journey that Yusuf was given half of all beauty.

outline.heading: 'I tried to seduce him and he held firm'
outline.gist: She admits he refused completely, though he had every reason to give in: young, a slave with no family to shame, pursued, behind closed doors. He sought refuge in Allah and would not betray his master.

outline.heading: Threatened with prison, pursued by all
outline.gist: Now she threatens him with long imprisonment and humiliation while the other women pursue him too, which he sees as the peak of chastity in the story.

outline.heading: 'Prison is dearer to me'
outline.gist: Yusuf tells Allah that prison is more beloved to him than what they call him to, and asks for help lest he weaken.

outline.heading: How far our ethics have drifted
outline.gist: Muslims today joke that they would serve a year in jail for a night with someone, the reverse of Yusuf's choice, without noticing how far they have strayed.

outline.heading: Why the rules between the sexes exist
outline.gist: Yusuf asked for help because desire is hard to control; that is why we lower our gaze, avoid being alone together and keep talk purposeful. Texting is a private one-on-one, so keep such chats in groups.

outline.heading: When young people lose control
outline.gist: Breaking these rules lets emotions build until couples feel they must marry despite being incompatible and too young, heading toward divorce.

outline.heading: Years in prison without regret
outline.gist: Accused and shamed publicly, Yusuf spent the better part of a decade in prison in his youth without bitterness and refused to leave until his name was cleared.

outline.heading: 'My paradise is in my chest'
outline.gist: A saying claimed for many scholars: enemies cannot touch my inner garden; prison is time alone with Allah, exile is travel, and death for my belief is martyrdom.

outline.heading: Do not spoil your chastity by wishing for haram
outline.gist: Young people who avoid zina should not ruin it by fantasising; if you keep wishing for it Allah may open the gates, and you will find it empty and damaging to your conscience.

outline.heading: It is fine to love some verses more
outline.gist: Keeping a list of verses you feel attached to is encouraged; the Prophet once spent a whole night repeating a single ayah.

outline.heading: Interlude
Learning from the verses that move others
outline.gist: People taste the Quran differently, so sharing the verses that move us teaches each of us something we had missed.

outline.heading: Yusuf's story ends with 'This is my way'
outline.gist: After the whole story of a man betrayed, enslaved and jailed who stayed upright and forgave his family, Allah tells the Prophet to declare his path.

outline.heading: Calling to Allah with insight and serenity
outline.gist: Basirah means calling with clarity and calm, without fear or inner doubt; this is the way of the Prophet and all who follow him.

outline.heading: Abu Sufyan seeks a way back
outline.gist: The Prophet lived the Quran. Before the conquest of Mecca, Abu Sufyan rode behind al-Abbas, afraid because he had lied to the Prophet's face, and asked Ali what to say.

outline.heading: Ali teaches him the words of Yusuf's brothers
outline.gist: Ali had him memorise what Yusuf's brothers said, knowing the Prophet would answer as Yusuf did: no blame on you today, Allah will forgive you.

outline.heading: The Prophet answers as Yusuf did
outline.gist: The Prophet named the lie, then forgave him and still called him to Islam, and Abu Sufyan wept at his generosity: calm and clear while others were lost.

outline.heading: Hearts find rest in Allah's remembrance
outline.gist: Believers' hearts settle through His name, His book and gatherings about Him, the opposite of the restless, anxious heart.

outline.heading: A natural calm: what the masjid is for
outline.gist: Reciting His words calms you without anything bought from a store; after a bad day you come to the masjid, pray and greet your brother, and feel better.

outline.heading: Facing problems with a calm heart
outline.gist: Anxious people make problems worse; even when the outcome is bad you choose how to meet it, and only remembrance of Allah gives the heart that calm.
